solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Profit about to go up

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
to shin up is to climb a pole or tree

explanation.surface: A trader learns the latest returns are set to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To profit from something is to cash in on it, turning an opportunity into gain.

clue.text: Patience maybe displayed by manager in firm with rising ambition

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: in places the manager's word inside the other
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: aim is an ambition or goal
a coper is one who copes, i.e. manages

explanation.surface: An ambitious manager at a firm shows patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patience' looks like a virtue, but it is a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a light, humorous Gilbert and Sullivan work, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Father gets new warning

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A dad receives a fresh caution.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm such as a police or air-raid wail is a warning signal.

clue.text: Reserve shown by old company head

parts.note: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British industrial giant
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A former firm's boss is notably standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British company until 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in manner is coldness or aloofness, a frosty quality.

clue.text: Superior points he passed on by mistake

parts.note: S and N are compass points, south and north
OB is short for obiit, Latin for 'he (or she) died', seen in obituaries
bish is old British schoolboy slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone haughty claims a dead man made his points in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the pieces. BISH is dated British slang for a mistake, and OB comes from Latin obiit.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior manner is condescending, looking down on others as inferior.

clue.text: Grounded winger with United after end of season

indicators.note: after puts the pieces for with and United behind the season's last letter
end of picks the final letter of season

parts.note: and means with, together
U is the usual abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A footballer for United is out injured once the season ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests football; it is a bird with wings, and grounded because it cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The nandu, or rhea, is a flightless South American bird, a winged creature unable to fly.

clue.text: Page from battered Hello devoured by bachelor quietly

indicators.note: devoured by means the mixed letters are swallowed between the outer pieces

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: battered means the word is knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A bachelor quietly scoffs a battered copy of Hello! magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine, so 'Page' seems to be from it; it is a hotel porter.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a boy employed to run errands, as a hotel porter does.

clue.text: Landlord to observe in secret

indicators.note: in tells us one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: inner can mean private or secret, as in inner thoughts
to keep a rule or festival is to observe it

explanation.surface: A landlord spies on his tenants covertly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's landlord is the person who runs the inn or tavern.

clue.text: Angry motorist may give off stink!

definitions.meaning: a furious driver sounds the car horn in a loud blast
British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A furious driver may also leave a bad smell behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A car horn's blast is one sense; British slang for a pong or stench is the other.

clue.text: Is inclined to go after success — lots available to offers?

indicators.note: to go after puts the leaning word behind the success word

parts.note: a hit is a success
a ship that lists is leaning, inclined

explanation.surface: An auction where items lean towards success after offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' and 'offers' suggest an auction; offers are killers (those who off people) and lots are their targets.
explanation.definitionFit: Assassins' rosters of intended victims are the people marked for killing.

clue.text: American doing bodywork's talked of additional painting

indicators.note: talked of says the phrase is spoken, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: more means additional, extra; a Titian is a painting by the Venetian master Titian

explanation.surface: A US panel-beater is said to want another Old Master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bodywork' suggests car repairs, but here the bodies are corpses: an American undertaker prepares the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortician is the US word for an undertaker, whose work is on dead bodies.

clue.text: Famous Red Square building's fourth from the right

indicators.note: reading from the right means the assembled letters are taken backwards

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

indicators.note: fourth points to the fourth letter of the word building

explanation.surface: It sounds like directions to the mausoleum on Moscow's Red Square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Square' looks like one place, but 'Red' belongs to the definition (a communist) and 'Square' is the number nine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshevik leader is the most famous communist, and Red is a common term for a communist.

clue.text: What's coming off a track as a result of cracks?

definitions.text: What's coming off a track as a result of cracks?

parts.words: What's coming off a track as a result of cracks?
parts.note: cracks are jokes and the track is a recorded soundtrack, so this is pre-recorded amusement played after the gags

explanation.surface: It sounds like a derailment caused by broken rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track' and 'cracks' suggest a railway accident; they are a sound recording and wisecracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded audience mirth is dubbed onto sitcom soundtracks in response to the jokes.

clue.text: Prefect's companion very keen to seize the day

indicators.note: to seize means one word grabs the other inside it

parts.note: ardent means passionately keen
Thur is short for Thursday

explanation.surface: A head pupil's eager friend is urged to seize the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prefect' looks like a school monitor; it is Ford Prefect from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Douglas Adams's comic novels the hapless Earthman travels with the alien Ford Prefect.

clue.text: Old journalist's vitality, say, returning on vacation

parts.note: pep is energy or vitality

indicators.note: returning means the letters left are turned back to front
on vacation means the word is emptied, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A veteran reporter's energy, say, comes back after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'journalist' here is a keeper of a journal: the 17th-century London diarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary, a daily journal, so he was a journalist in that old sense.

clue.text: Something held against conflict that's dragged on

definitions.text: Something held against conflict that's dragged on

parts.words: Something held against conflict that's dragged on
parts.note: a tobacco pipe one drags on, smoked as a token against war

explanation.surface: It reads like a protest held against a war that has dragged on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dragged on' suggests a long war; it is drawing on a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The calumet was smoked by Native Americans to seal treaties and goodwill.

clue.text: Smoother and sounder without ultimate in bland drivel

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the saner letters surround the rest

parts.note: sounder in mind is saner

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the last letter of bland

parts.note: pap is trivial, insipid stuff

explanation.surface: A smoother and saner voice, minus the end of some boring nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without ultimate' looks like 'drop the last letter', but 'without' means outside and 'ultimate in' picks the D of bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive paper is used to make wood or paint smooth, so it is a smoothing tool.

clue.text: Void seen after dizzying plunge

indicators.note: dizzying means the letters are sent spinning into a new order

explanation.surface: Peering into an abyss after a giddy plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep headlong descent, as of a plane or of prices, is a plunge.

clue.text: Record only small tunes again

parts.note: a meter is said to read, i.e. record, a value
just means only, merely

explanation.surface: A record with just a few short tunes is played once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune an instrument again is to adjust it afresh, setting it right once more.

clue.text: Shocking reminder that keeps army officer at home

indicators.note: that keeps says the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a jog to the memory is a reminder
LT is short for lieutenant
in means at home

explanation.surface: A shocking note that an army officer is confined to barracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something jarring or startling comes as a sudden shock.

clue.text: The girl, alas, in retreat, letting out the odd cry

indicators.note: in retreat means the letters chosen are read going backwards
letting out the odd letters keeps only the even ones of the phrase

explanation.surface: A girl retreating with a lament lets out a strange shout.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'The girl alas' are H, G, R, A, A; read back they make the cry.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of frustration or horror is a kind of cry or scream.

clue.text: Another thing entirely, indeed, involving guerrilla army resistance

indicators.note: involving means the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: ay, or aye, means yes indeed
FARC was the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Guerrilla resistance is quite another matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something very different from what it is compared with.

clue.text: Reason for buoyancy in floodgate, set loose with force

indicators.note: set loose means the letters are freed to form a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Water bursting through a floodgate with force keeps things afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buoyancy' suggests floating in the flood, but it is economic or emotional optimism.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names whatever lifts public mood and confidence, i.e. buoyant spirits.

clue.text: Welshman maybe removing hat, revealing ear?

indicators.note: removing hat in a down clue drops the top letter of the name

parts.note: Morgan is a typical Welsh name

explanation.surface: A Welshman doffs his cap and shows his ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear is one example of a body part with a specific function.

clue.text: Cheers enveloping Irish after clinching a triple crown

indicators.note: enveloping means the thanks word wraps round the rest

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers

indicators.note: clinching means the Irish abbreviation holds the letter between its two

explanation.surface: Irish rugby fans cheer winning the Triple Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby Triple Crown goes to a home nation beating the other three; the definition is the Pope's three-tiered crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal headdress has three tiers, making it a crown of three crowns.

clue.text: It follows higher course to start with?

parts.note: so means therefore, it follows
up means higher

explanation.surface: Something comes after a higher course of study to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of broth is often the first course, or starter, of a meal.

clue.text: Poet's eye in the end caught by two antelopes

indicators.note: the final letter of the poet's word is taken in by the two strokes that follow

parts.note: orb is a poetic word for an eye
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A poet glimpses a pair of antelopes at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end caught by two' sends the last letter of the poetic eye inside the Roman two. The plural of this antelope is the same as the singular, so 'antelopes' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope; the same word serves as its plural.

clue.text: Extraordinarily, achieves first in geography — follow that!

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of geography
extraordinarily means the letters are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Someone tops the geography class and dares the rest to match it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow that!' looks like a boast; it is the order a detective barks: pursue it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue a fleeing car or person is to go after them, as in 'Follow that car!'

clue.text: Play part with inner energy note to the end

indicators.note: with inner says the second word sits inside the first
to the end says one letter is shifted to the final position of the word

explanation.surface: An actor puts inner energy into a role, saving one note for the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is N, but it is the N already in 'energy' that 'to the end' shifts last; 'with inner' then sets the result inside the abbreviation for part.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's verse drama about a Norwegian wanderer is a famous stage work.

clue.text: Authoritarian deputy ran the shows

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display within the run of words

explanation.surface: A deputy took charge of the productions.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot or bully wielding absolute power is an authoritarian figure.
